content.comment_body: Hello everyone, does anyone know why only the [product_name] with [version_no] is suitable for this project? I don't require any of the advanced features from this version. *** Determine [product_name] Resources used: Function Blocks 40/400 REM 0/250 Digital Inputs 4/24 Digital Outputs 4/16 Flag 2/27 Analog Inputs 0/8 Text Box 6/50 Text contents 6/50 Analog outputs 0/2 Program memory 580/8000 Block names 0/100 Analog flags 1/16 Cursor keys 0/4 Shift register 0/4 Shift register bits 0/32 Open connectors 0/64 [product_name] TD Function keys 0/4 Network inputs 0/64 Network analog inputs 0/32 UDF types 0/16 UDF instances 0/64 Data Log 0/1 Network outputs 0/64 Network analog outputs 0/16 Analog Filters 0/8 Maximum nesting depth: I1-B008-B037-B006-B010-B023-B004-B041-Q1 The following [product_name] version can be used: [article_no].Standard Thanks in advance!
Hi, You are likely using a feature that isn't available in older versions of [product_name]. Share the program so we can identify which feature it is.

Thanks for your help, [user_name]. I've attached the diagram. It’s strange because I created the program using [version_no], but after moving it to a newer version, it only works there. The project isn't completely done yet.

If you adjust the TEXT blocks, you may be able to use earlier versions like [article_no]. Try this at home: F2 (TOOLS > Determine [product_name]), check the Info screen and scroll up. There you'll see which [product_name] hardware is compatible and the reason older hardware doesn't fit. You can also see what's wrong in your program. You can't transfer it to the hardware because some blocks, like the text blocks, aren't connected. Every block in [product_name] must have an output. You can use the Open Connector block for that. Next time, start a new program and begin by choosing the correct hardware in the software (CTRL+H, TOOLS > Select Hardware). This helps prevent compatibility issues.

Thank you, [user_name]. I'm aware that the program currently can't run on all versions of the hardware yet, but that's not my main concern. Removing text blocks still doesn't allow compatibility with [article_no]. Got it! The [Select Hardware] feature clarified which blocks are not supported by older versions such as [article_no]. I’ll work around the limitations. Thanks, [user_name]!

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered compatibility issues when moving projects between different hardware versions of [product_name]. Although a program was originally made in an earlier version, opening and editing it in a newer version made it incompatible with previous models. Even after removing some features, the compatibility problem remained, highlighting complexities in version control and hardware selection.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to be able to develop and update projects while keeping them compatible with older hardware versions, as long as new, exclusive features are not used.
